result.topic_en: Formula-only calculations with square roots of products of quadratic and linear factors in x, y, z (an addition-theorem-type relation), followed by manipulations of radical identities in letters p, q, u, v, t and auxiliary quantities f, φ, ψ.
result.transcription:
$\partial z\sqrt{(x+y+z)^2+mxy} + \sqrt{(x-\alpha z)(x-\beta z)(y-\gamma z)(y-\delta z)} = xy + z(ax+by+cz) [-+\sqrt{(x+y+z)^2+mxy}-]$
$= xy + zq$
$\partial z\sqrt{xy+p^2}$
$[-\partial^2 z^2 (x+y+z)^2-]$

$\partial^2 z^2(xy+p^2) + (x-\alpha z)(x-\beta z)(y-\gamma z)(y-\delta z) - (xy+zq)^2 = \sqrt{\quad}\sqrt{\quad}$
$2\partial z$
$x^2+2axz+bz^2 \quad y^2+2a'yz+b'z^2$
$x^2y^2 + y^2(2ax+bz) + x^2(2a'y+b'z)$

$\partial^2 z(xy+p^2) + y^2(2ax+bz) + x^2(2a'y+b'z) + z(2ax+bz)(2a'y+b'z)$
$-2xyq - zq^2$

$q-v=q' \quad = 2\partial\sqrt{(x^2+2axz+bz^2)(y^2+2a'yz+b'z^2)(xy+p^2)}$
$(q-v)\sqrt{up} [-=-] \alpha\sqrt{p'q'uq} - \beta\sqrt{p'q'pv}$
$\sqrt{q'up'} = \alpha\sqrt{p'uq} - \beta\sqrt{p'pv}$
$f^2 = uv\,pq\,t$
$\varphi^2 = uv\,p'q'\,t$
$\psi^2 = pq\,p'q'\,t$

$(f-\alpha\varphi)(f+\alpha\varphi) = uv(pq-\alpha^2p'q')t$

$u(pq-\alpha^2p'q') + vt = 2\sqrt{uvpqt}$
$\sqrt{upq} [-+-] \sqrt{vt}$ [?] $= \alpha\sqrt{p'q'u}$
$\sqrt{puv} - \sqrt{qt} = \beta\sqrt{p'q'p}$

$f+\alpha\varphi = [-u-](pq-\alpha^2p'q')$
$f-\alpha\varphi = [-v-]\,t$
$f+\beta\psi = [-p-](uv-\beta^2p'q')$
$f-\beta\psi = [-q-]\,t$
$\beta\psi-\alpha\varphi = [-(v-q)t-]$
$= (v-q)t$

$v-q=q'$
